TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx FINANCIAL AID Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units. EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration TEST CREDIT If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit TRANSFER HELP Do you have questions about your transfer work? We are located in the Office of the Registrar , on the first floor of University Hall ( interactive map link ).

This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details.


TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: MAJOR INFORMATION The Bachelor of Arts in Music Therapy is a four-year plus internship undergraduate degree that prepares students to be leaders among their communities in the field of music therapy. Music Therapy is an allied health profession in which music interventions are used to address therapeutic or palliative care needs. Our program is designed to generate an understanding of music, human development and exceptionality, clinical practice, and the music therapy process through classroom experience and clinical training in local and community-based settings. This degree provides not only required core courses in music, clinical studies, and music therapy practice--thereby providing the professional competencies required by the American Music Therapy Association (AMTA)--but also 1200 hours of supervised clinical training (at least 900 of which are completed through the internship process). Completing this degree will prepare students to sit for the certification exam with the Certification Board for Music Therapists (the MT-BC credential). ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://catalog.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/music/music-therapy-ba/ ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES **CLASS PIANO REQUIREMENT: The piano proficiency (class piano) requirement can also be met by successful completion of credit by examination administered by the department. **AREA OF STUDY: Students must complete four lower-division units in the SAME instrument/area of study. **ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible. ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) This major does not have a corresponding Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT).

MAJOR INFORMATION

The Bachelor of Arts in Music Therapy is a four-year plus internship undergraduate degree that prepares students to be leaders among their communities in the field of music therapy. Music Therapy is an allied health profession in which music interventions are used to address therapeutic or palliative care needs. Our program is designed to generate an understanding of music, human development and exceptionality, clinical practice, and the music therapy process through classroom experience and clinical training in local and community-based settings.


This degree provides not only required core courses in music, clinical studies, and music therapy practice--thereby providing the professional competencies required by the American Music Therapy Association (AMTA)--but also 1200 hours of supervised clinical training (at least 900 of which are completed through the internship process). Completing this degree will prepare students to sit for the certification exam with the Certification Board for Music Therapists (the MT-BC credential).


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: https://catalog.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/arts-letters/music/music-therapy-ba/


ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES

**CLASS PIANO REQUIREMENT: The piano proficiency (class piano) requirement can also be met by successful completion of credit by examination administered by the department.

**AREA OF STUDY: Students must complete four lower-division units in the SAME instrument/area of study.

**ARTICULATES AS A SERIES ONLY: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible.


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

This major does not have a corresponding Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT).
